messages:
incident-bot: [PagerDuty] page fired — service=model-catalog-service code=CATALOG_PIN_MISMATCH severity=P1
pagerduty: Incident 90102 triggered, routing to eng-oncall
maria.chen: ack — oncall here, pulling logs and recent catalog writes
devon.patel: ack, can we get customer impact quickly? any 5xx spike?
incident-bot: Observability: 5xx spike between 18:12:05Z and 18:22:40Z. "tokenizer_error: vocab_incompatible(-1)" seen in 14% of requests; spike concentrated on routes using open-6b.default
liam.oconnor: looking at router traces — some hosts load tokenizer rev13 while client metadata indicates rev18. mismatch occurs when pinned_rev != default_rev and pin flow is partially applied
maria.chen: did a catalog promote earlier this morning; looks like pin_rev was set for canary tenants but default_rev remained older. router rollout didn't catch the pin metadata in all rings
devon.patel: impact breakdown by tenant from last 10m: alpha-prod 31%, beta-int 2%, gamma 0.8%, delta-pro 47%. delta-pro is heavy long-context (makes sense)
maria.chen: mitigation options: 1) immediate catalog rollback of pin_rev for canaries (fast, but kills canary), 2) apply per-tenant route override to enforce pinned rev for both tokenizer+weights, 3) introduce a compatibility shim to map token IDs (risky)
devon.patel: prefer non-destructive route override first. we have /internal/v1/route-override and can target affected routers by tenant tag
maria.chen: executing override for delta-pro and alpha-prod now
```
curl -s -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/route-override -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SRE_TOKEN}" -d '{"tenant":"delta-pro","model":"open-6b","override":{"enforce_pin_consistency":true}}'
```
incident-bot: route-override accepted (ro=10021). change streaming to router fleet (rolling). applying to 24 nodes
liam.oconnor: watching logs — errors for delta-pro drop within ~40s
sre-oncall: note: some routers show stale KV cache leading to transient mismatches after override. recommend KV cache restart for router-group-3
maria.chen: can we do a graceful KV cache restart? that will drain sessions briefly
devon.patel: yes, use /internal/admin/graceful_kv_restart?group=router-group-3&drain_secs=25
maria.chen: kicking it off now
incident-bot: kvc-restart job queued (job=kr-334). restart started at 18:19:40Z, expected drain 25s
liam.oconnor: post-restart, delta-pro error rate down to 4%. overall system error rate down to 2.1%
devon.patel: starting conference bridge with CS and affected customer rep for delta-pro @ 18:25Z to inform them and collect repros
cs-lead: joining bridge. I'll prepare an impact note with time window and mitigation steps. please include retries guidance for SDKs
maria.chen: deploying a small catalog-service change to validate pin_rev/default_rev compatibility on write and emit a warning metric. will stage to canary tomorrow
devon.patel: thanks. keep route override for now until validation is live. create follow-up ticket for a hard-fail option on incompatible pins
eng-runtime-oncall: taking handoff for next 4 hours. escalation plan: if tokenizer_mismatch_rate >5% for >10m, rollback pin_rev across canaries
pagerduty: severity downgraded to P2 at 18:28:12Z — reduced impact and stable mitigations
maria.chen: drafting post-incident summary: timeframe 18:12:05Z-18:28:12Z (mitigated), affected tenants: alpha-prod, delta-pro primarily; cause: catalog pin/default inconsistency leading to tokenizer/weights misalignment across router fleet; mitigations: per-tenant route-override + graceful KV cache restart; follow-ups: write-time validation, router startup sync, telemetry metric for tokenizer_mismatch_count
sre-oncall: logging follow-up tasks into JIRA: INF-4729 (validation), INF-4730 (router sync), INF-4731 (alert rule)
maria.chen: leaving overrides in place for safety. handing off to eng-runtime-oncall (monitoring dashboard pinned). will reconvene once validation patch is deployed
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident 90102 resolved (auto) at 18:29:05Z — keeping thread open for follow-ups
maria.chen: thx all. postmortem draft incoming. :v:
